neighbours.label: a degree word (so, too, not too, particularly) about to name a bad quality, when the context is critical; the same word in praise stays quiet
fire: The graphics are dated, and the controls are so clumsy.
The plot drags, and the jokes are too flat.
The hotel was dirty, and the staff were particularly rude.
Steel is so heavy that a truck would need a bigger engine.
The soup was bland, and surprisingly not too hot.
The seats are hard, and the screen is so dim.
The battery dies fast, and the case is too flimsy.
The film is dull, and the ending is particularly weak.
quiet: The graphics are lovely, and the controls are so smooth.
The plot flies, and the jokes are really sharp.
The hotel was spotless, and the staff were particularly kind.
Silver is so pretty that a ring would make a fine gift.
The soup was rich, and surprisingly very fresh.
The seats are soft, and the screen is so bright.
The battery lasts long, and the case is very sturdy.
The film is gripping, and the ending is particularly moving.

notes: Probes: 'the people were so friendly' 0.003 against 'the menus are so slow' 0.47. 'just as unhealthy' and 'just as delicious' both scored 0.05, so 'just as' is left out.
